question: Can frozen metric depth plus runtime-equivalent pose/gravity recover parent-disjoint two-sided obstacle evidence through deterministic height geometry?

protocol.pose_role: runtime-equivalent VIO/IMU observable; not source depth or factor outcome

pose_analytic_geometry.interpretation: Only half the parents produced a persistent predicted-depth plane and a policy-valid camera height in all three frames. Two additional ARKit parents crossed the 2.20 m camera-height ceiling in one frame, and one ARKit parent had no admissible persistent mode.

result.interpretation: Adding pose/gravity did recover complete analytic geometry for three parents, but the resulting obstacle ranking conflicted with source-valid obstacle labels on every training roster: even the most conservative low and high grid endpoints violated the per-parent error caps. Pose observability is therefore not the remaining bottleneck; predicted-depth scale/plane fidelity is insufficient for this task factor.

decision.reopen_condition: Acquire or freeze genuinely new source-native obstacle supervision or a materially different representation that directly improves metric-depth scale/plane fidelity. Any future route must start with a new protocol and consumed/fresh role assignment; it may not retune the three failed obstacle candidates.

claim_boundary: Consumed six-parent Development evidence that pose-anchored deterministic height geometry does not rescue the current frozen metric-depth obstacle factor. Together with the scalar and nested-interaction terminals, this closes the present AG obstacle-to-task landing route. It does not establish general impossibility, independent cross-sensor performance, deployment, product readiness, default-App eligibility, navigation utility or assistive safety.
